title: Rosa Parks's birth chart
metaDescription: Rosa Parks's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.3° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled fall in fixed signs, the widest weighting the unknown hour leaves certain. The fixed signs are the scheme’s ballast — mid-season, fully committed, expensive to turn.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 15.3° Aquarius. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mercury in the classical scheme — an air sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aquarius (9.4°), Venus in Aries (1.9°), Mars in Capricorn (18.9°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Venus a sixth of the circle apart from Uranus, 2.3° off exact. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Saturn sextile Neptune at 3.1°, and Venus square Pluto at 3.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aquarius at 15.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Aries at 1.9° is in detriment; Mars in Capricorn at 18.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Capricorn at 7.2° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 air, 3 earth, 1 fire, 1 water; by modality, 4 fixed, 4 cardinal, 1 mutable. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.0° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
